newsitem.title: USA: US Sen. Lott - budget plan has votes in committee.
newsitem.headline: US Sen. Lott - budget plan has votes in committee.

text.p: A budget resolution expected to be considered by the Senate Budget Committee Thursday has the votes to pass that committee, Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said Wednesday.
Lott told reporters the committee would probably take up the budget framework Thursday even if remaining differences with the White House were not fully worked out.
"We have the votes to get it out of the budget committee, but we want to get it in a bipartisan way," the Mississippi Republican said.

Lott said he hoped to have the budget resolution put before the Senate for a vote early next week. The resolution is essentially a budget blueprint that Congress must pass before taking up legislation to enact details of the budget.
Legislation to enact the details is known as "reconciliation," and Lott said it was unclear whether the Senate could do separate reconciliation bills on spending and taxes because of a Senate rule.
White House Legislative Director John Hilley had earlier said agreement had been reached for there to be separate bills so there would be separate votes on spending and taxes.

A letter outlining the agreement on tax cuts being drafted by congressional leaders to President Clinton will state that up to $35 billion would be considered in the budget for education tax credits that Clinton is seeking, Lott said.
The letter would not include details of a capital gains tax cut, he said.
The Republican chairmen of the congressional tax-writing committees have been adamant about wanting to write the details of the tax provisions in their committees.
"I have said emphatically from the beginning, we are not going to write the tax bill in any kind of side agreement," Lott said.

"The president's insisted on his education provision in there, and we have an obligation I think to try to help get that in a form that he can live with, but beyond that we are not agreeing to any limits -- not on capital gains, not on estate tax," Lott said.
